mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate directly reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the cost of capital declines.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns show no positive correlation with FEDFUNDS changes (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 3.0%, the Federal Reserve is expected to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as equity valuations contract under higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p < 0.05) in periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0% yoy, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and a reduction in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a coordinated policy response to a weakening economy, which typically precedes a 5-day positive S&P 500 return as investors anticipate further stimulus and economic support.
regime_hint: monetary policy easing with housing weakness
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining HOUST and falling FEDFUNDS fails to predict positive 5-day SPX returns in more than 40% of instances (i.e., positive returns occur in < 60% of cases), or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 7.5%), the S&P 500 tends to underperform as economic weakness signals reduced corporate earnings growth, leading to negative 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p < 0.05) when UNRATE exceeds 7.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns show no positive correlation with PAYEMS growth (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1400.0 thousand units signals weakening consumer demand for housing, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as economic growth concerns mount.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p < 0.05) when HOUST falls below 1400.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 1-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a contraction in real GDP (GDPC1) signals a severe economic slowdown, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as recession fears intensify.
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining INDPRO and GDPC1 fails to predict negative 60-day SPX returns in more than 40% of instances (i.e., negative returns occur in < 60% of cases), or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a period of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100.0), the S&P 500 tends to experience negative 20-day forward returns as manufacturing weakness signals a broad economic slowdown and reduced corporate profitability.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p < 0.05) when INDPRO falls below 100.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.
